Deliver Guarantee
blocks.text: Deliver Guarantee

blocks.html: A delivery guarantee describes what can happen to an event when failures and retries occur.
blocks.text: A delivery guarantee describes what can happen to an event when failures and retries occur.

blocks.html: An event may be missed, processed again, or have its result recorded exactly once, depending on how the system handles failures.
blocks.text: An event may be missed, processed again, or have its result recorded exactly once, depending on how the system handles failures.

blocks.html: The examples below focus on a consumer processing records already stored in Kafka. Reliable publication and storage also depend on producer and broker settings.
blocks.text: The examples below focus on a consumer processing records already stored in Kafka. Reliable publication and storage also depend on producer and broker settings.

blocks.html: Processing an event and saving the next offset are separate actions unless they are coordinated. A crash between them creates the main problem.
blocks.text: Processing an event and saving the next offset are separate actions unless they are coordinated. A crash between them creates the main problem.

blocks.html: At-most-once
blocks.text: At-most-once

blocks.html: A record is processed zero or one time. It can be skipped after a failure.
blocks.text: A record is processed zero or one time. It can be skipped after a failure.

blocks.html: Assume a consumer saves the next offset before processing the current record.
blocks.text: Assume a consumer saves the next offset before processing the current record.

blocks.html: If it crashes before processing, it resumes after that record. The work is missed even though the record may still exist in Kafka.
blocks.text: If it crashes before processing, it resumes after that record. The work is missed even though the record may still exist in Kafka.

blocks.html: This avoids retrying that record, but does not remove duplicate business events that were already published.
blocks.text: This avoids retrying that record, but does not remove duplicate business events that were already published.

blocks.html: At-least-once
blocks.text: At-least-once

blocks.html: A record is processed one or more times. Retries can repeat the work.
blocks.text: A record is processed one or more times. Retries can repeat the work.

blocks.html: The consumer processes a record first, then saves the next offset.
blocks.text: The consumer processes a record first, then saves the next offset.

blocks.html: If processing succeeds but the consumer crashes before saving progress, it reads the record again after restarting.
blocks.text: If processing succeeds but the consumer crashes before saving progress, it reads the record again after restarting.

blocks.html: Let us say processing sends an email. The first email may already have been sent, so retrying can send it again.
blocks.text: Let us say processing sends an email. The first email may already have been sent, so retrying can send it again.

blocks.html: This requires retrying unfinished work while the input records remain available, along with suitable publication and storage settings.
blocks.text: This requires retrying unfinished work while the input records remain available, along with suitable publication and storage settings.

blocks.html: Exactly-once
blocks.text: Exactly-once

blocks.html: The intended result is recorded once, even if processing is attempted again after a failure.
blocks.text: The intended result is recorded once, even if processing is attempted again after a failure.

blocks.html: For an application that reads from Kafka and writes results back to Kafka, a Kafka transaction can save the output records and the next input offsets together.
blocks.text: For an application that reads from Kafka and writes results back to Kafka, a Kafka transaction can save the output records and the next input offsets together.

blocks.html: A transaction makes these changes succeed together or leaves neither committed.
blocks.text: A transaction makes these changes succeed together or leaves neither committed.

blocks.html: If it commits, the output and saved progress are both recorded. If it aborts, the application can retry from the saved input position.
blocks.text: If it commits, the output and saved progress are both recorded. If it aborts, the application can retry from the saved input position.

blocks.html: Downstream consumers must be configured to read committed transactional records. Correct transaction and recovery settings are required.
blocks.text: Downstream consumers must be configured to read committed transactional records. Correct transaction and recovery settings are required.

blocks.html: This does not automatically cover an email, payment, or update in an external database. Those actions need coordination with the destination system.
blocks.text: This does not automatically cover an email, payment, or update in an external database. Those actions need coordination with the destination system.

blocks.html: Making retries safe
blocks.text: Making retries safe

blocks.html: An idempotent operation produces the same intended result when the same request is repeated.
blocks.text: An idempotent operation produces the same intended result when the same request is repeated.

blocks.html: For a database update, the application can save a unique event ID and the update in one database transaction. On retry, it checks the ID and avoids applying the update again.
blocks.text: For a database update, the application can save a unique event ID and the update in one database transaction. On retry, it checks the ID and avoids applying the update again.

blocks.html: For an email or payment API, safe retries may use an idempotency key if the provider supports it. The same key identifies retries of the same operation.
blocks.text: For an email or payment API, safe retries may use an idempotency key if the provider supports it. The same key identifies retries of the same operation.

blocks.html: Kafka producer idempotence prevents duplicate records from supported producer send retries. It does not by itself prevent repeated consumer actions or duplicate business events sent as new requests.
